Flash attention

Source: R/flash.R
zl_flash_attention.Rd

zl_flash_attention() computes softmax(scale * t(k) %*% q + mask) weighted sums of v for every query, head and batch, in one fused operation that holds no matrix of scores, so long contexts attend in memory linear in their length. It is 'ggml”s ggml_flash_attn_ext.

Usage

zl_flash_attention(q, k, v, mask = NULL, scale = 1)

Arguments

q, k, v

Tensors.

mask

NULL, or a tensor added to the scores.

scale

The factor applied to the scores before the mask, usually 1 / sqrt(d).

Value

A tensor.

Details

The layouts are 'ggml”s: q is c(d, n, heads, batch), k is c(d, n_kv, heads_kv, batch) and v is c(d_v, n_kv, heads_kv, batch), not transposed; heads_kv must divide heads. The result is c(d_v, heads, n, batch), heads before positions, so that zl_reshape(o, c(d_v * heads, n, batch)) joins the heads. Trailing dimensions of 1 may be left out of the inputs; the result has at least three.

The mask is added to the scaled scores. It is c(n_kv, n), optionally with third and fourth dimensions that divide heads and batch. The kernel reads it in half precision: 0 and -Inf are exact, other values are rounded to about three significant digits.

The operation has no gradient, so a graph that trains through it is refused; zl_softmax() and zl_crossprod() give the same attention with gradients. Results agree with that plain form to within f32 rounding, and do not depend on zl_threads(): a single query, which 'ggml' would split across threads by key, is computed as two identical queries so that each stays on one thread.

Examples

p <- zl_params()
g <- zl_graph(
  function(x) zl_flash_attention(x$q, x$k, x$v, scale = 1 / 2),
  p,
  inputs = list(q = c(4, 3, 2), k = c(4, 5, 2), v = c(4, 5, 2))
)
dim(zl_forward(g, list(
  q = array(1, c(4, 3, 2)), k = array(1, c(4, 5, 2)), v = array(1, c(4, 5, 2))
))$output)
#> [1] 4 2 3
